name: How do I make an outdoor entertainment area feel private in a dense neighborhood?

mainEntity.name: How can I make an outdoor entertainment area private in a neighborhood with close lots, second-story windows, or street visibility?
mainEntity.text: How can I make an outdoor entertainment area private in a neighborhood with close lots, second-story windows, or street visibility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Privacy in a dense Los Angeles neighborhood usually works best when several elements do the job together. Start by identifying the main sightlines from neighboring windows, upper floors, or the street. Then use layered screening such as hedges, trellises, slatted fences, privacy panels, and tall planters. A pergola can also create a more enclosed feeling overhead without fully closing the space in. Place the main seating area where views are naturally blocked, and avoid putting the most used zone directly in the line of sight. Sound also affects privacy, so water features, soft landscaping, and thoughtful speaker placement can help the space feel more secluded. The goal is not to make the yard feel boxed in, but to make guests feel comfortable using it without constantly being on display.
acceptedAnswer.description: Privacy comes from layered screening, not one single barrier. Plantings, slatted walls, pergolas, tall planters, and carefully placed seating can block sightlines while keeping the space open and attractive.
